title: bug: moe-agent.sh subagent mirror races when two seats start in one project (cp EEXIST under set -e kills pre-flight)
description: Repro (WT-19b trial, scripts/tests/worktree-e2e.cjs, two worker seats launched at once into a fresh control checkout): seat b exits 1 in pre-flight with `cp: cannot create regular file '<project>/.claude/agents/moe-code-reviewer.md': File exists`. Cause: scripts/moe-agent.sh:2130-2134 checks `[ -e "$dest" ]` and then runs a plain `cp "$src" "$dest"` under `set -e`; GNU cp opens a missing destination with O_EXCL, so the seat that loses the race dies (ps1 uses `Copy-Item -Force` and keeps going). Fix: tolerate EEXIST (`cp "$src" "$dest" 2>/dev/null || [ -e "$dest" ] || <fail>`) and count it as kept. Until then, WT-19b's fixture pre-seeds <control>/.claude/agents, which is the live checkout's state.
definitionOfDone: Two moe-agent.sh seats starting at the same moment in one project both pass the subagent mirror (a postflight.sh arm, or a loop of concurrent mirrors, reproduces it before the fix and passes after)
A destination that another seat created between the -e check and the copy counts as kept, not as a failure

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (RED) — DoD 1 and 2. Create scripts/tests/subagent-mirror.test.mjs (node:test, ESM; Write tool) and wire it into CI. It runs the wrappers' REAL subagent-mirror block, sliced out by anchor text, so no product refactor is needed. Copy the conventions of scripts/tests/seat-registration.test.mjs:
- read ../moe-agent.sh and ../moe-agent.ps1 via new URL(…, import.meta.url), drop a leading U+FEFF, CRLF->LF;
- between(source, start, end) and fwd/shq/psq;
- the ENGINES table + probe(): bash (or 'C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe' on Windows), PowerShell 5.1 Windows-only, PowerShell 7 probed, each with a skip reason;
- delete MOE_WORKER_ID, MOE_PROJECT_PATH and MOE_SESSION_ID from the child env.

SLICES. Start anchor (unique in both wrappers today): '# Mirror .moe/agents/<name>.md to .claude/agents/<name>.md so Claude Code's'. End anchors: sh '\nLOOP_ENABLED=false', ps1 '# Normalize Command + CommandArgs'. Assert each slice contains its copy call (sh 'cp "$src"', ps1 'Copy-Item'), so a moved anchor fails loudly. Child script = preamble + optional injection + slice + a sentinel line printing '@@ after mirror'.
- sh, run as bash --noprofile --norc <file>: set -e; GREEN=''; NC=''; RED=''; YELLOW=''; ENABLE_AGENT_TEAMS=true; PROJECT=<fwd path>; MOE_DIR="$PROJECT/.moe".
- ps1, run as -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <file>: write it with a leading \ufeff BOM (mem:gotcha-ps51-bomless-non-ascii-needles; the slice holds a non-ASCII arrow). Preamble: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; $enableAgentTeams = $true; $projectPath = <path>; $moeDir = Join-Path $projectPath '.moe'.
- Fixture per row: mkdtemp under os.tmpdir(); <project>/.moe/agents/one.md and two.md (distinct, >=1 KB); no .claude dir; rmSync(dir, {recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 5}) in finally.

ROWS, per engine unless noted:
A 'a copy that loses the race to another seat counts as kept'. Inject on one.md only.
- sh: a cp() shell function (it shadows the binary, and $(…) subshells inherit it). For 2 operands whose destination ends in /one.md, it runs `command cp "$1" "$2"` (the other seat's create lands), appends a line to $MIRROR_RACE_LOG, prints "cp: cannot create regular file '$2': File exists" to stderr and returns 1: GNU cp's lost O_EXCL create. Every other call is `command cp "$@"`.
- ps1: function Copy-Item (functions shadow cmdlets) with params [string]$Path, [string]$LiteralPath, [string]$Destination, [switch]$Force. For one.md it calls Microsoft.PowerShell.Management\Copy-Item -LiteralPath <whichever of LiteralPath/Path is set> -Destination $Destination -Force, appends to $env:MIRROR_RACE_LOG and throws [System.IO.IOException]::new("The process cannot access the file '$Destination' because it is being used by another process."). Otherwise it copies through the same module-qualified cmdlet. Use cmdlets, never [IO.File], on wrapper-built paths: pwsh on Linux resolves the wrapper's '.claude\agents' only through the provider.
- Assert: exit 0; output contains 'Subagents: mirrored 1, kept 1 existing (.moe/agents/ -> .claude/agents/)' and '@@ after mirror'; the race log has exactly 1 line; both .claude/agents files byte-equal their sources.
B 'any other copy failure still stops the pre-flight'. Inject on one.md WITHOUT creating it.
- sh prints "cp: cannot create regular file '$2': Permission denied" and returns 1.
- ps1 throws [System.UnauthorizedAccessException]::new("Access to the path '$Destination' is denied.").
- Assert: non-zero exit; stdout+stderr contain 'Permission denied' (sh) / 'is denied' (ps1); no '@@ after mirror'; .claude/agents/one.md absent.
C (bash engine only) 'two seats mirroring at the same moment both pass': the DoD's loop of concurrent mirrors, with the REAL cp.
- One bash driver (spawnSync, timeout 120 s) runs 30 rounds. Each round makes a fresh project with six agent files a.md..f.md (>=4 KB each).
- Each round starts two seat children running the slice behind a ready/go barrier: each child touches ready-<n> and spins until go exists; the driver creates go once both ready files exist. Every spin is bounded to 10 s.
- The driver waits on both by recorded PID. Never pkill/killall or name-matched kills (project rail).
- Assert: all 60 seat runs exit 0 and print the banner and the sentinel; every .claude/agents file byte-equals its source.
D 'the wrapper parses': sh `bash -n` on moe-agent.sh; ps1 [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile on moe-agent.ps1 with zero errors.

CI: append scripts/tests/subagent-mirror.test.mjs to the run line of the 'Test launcher daemon.json cap and seat re-registration' step in .github/workflows/ci.yml (build-all-platforms: Linux runs bash + pwsh 7, Windows Git Bash + PS 5.1 + pwsh 7). Keep its `if: runner.os != 'macOS'` byte-identical: daemon-json-cap.test.mjs's CI-guard test asserts that exact line.

RED evidence for the complete_step note (wrappers still unfixed): this is the DoD's 'reproduces it before the fix'.
- `node --test scripts/tests/subagent-mirror.test.mjs` fails bash rows A and C with 'File exists' and passes B and D; the PowerShell rows skip under WSL node.
- `"/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" --test "$(wslpath -w scripts/tests/subagent-mirror.test.mjs)"` (mem:gotcha-launcher-ps1-rows-from-wsl) also fails row A on both PowerShell engines with the IOException.
- The architect measured the unfixed loop on WSL ext4 losing 100 of 300 two-seat rounds, so 30 rounds miss the race with p≈5e-6.

implementationPlan.description:
FIX scripts/moe-agent.sh — DoD 1 and 2. Edit only the pre-flight mirror block under '# Mirror .moe/agents/<name>.md …' (~line 2118). Do NOT edit prepare_worktree_launch's `cp -f` into the task's own W, which no other seat shares.

Replace the bare `cp "$src" "$dest"` with:
        if ! AGENT_CP_ERR=$(cp "$src" "$dest" 2>&1); then
            if [ -e "$dest" ]; then
                AGENT_SKIPPED=$((AGENT_SKIPPED + 1))
                continue
            fi
            printf '%s\n' "$AGENT_CP_ERR" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
Keep `AGENT_MIRRORED=$((AGENT_MIRRORED + 1))` after it.

Comment the new lines:
- Two seats starting at the same moment both pass the -e check. GNU cp creates a missing destination with O_EXCL, so the seat whose create loses gets EEXIST for a file the other seat is writing from the same source. That file counts as kept (task-b6a3d41e).
- Error handling for a real failure is unchanged: with no destination, cp's own message is printed and the pre-flight exits 1, exactly as set -e did.
Amend the header's 'Idempotent: …' sentence: a destination another seat creates meanwhile is kept too.

Keep the first comment line (the test's start anchor), the banner and `LOOP_ENABLED=false` unchanged. Add no operator-visible string, so the parity vocabulary does not change.
Why capture stderr rather than the description's `2>/dev/null || [ -e ] || <fail>`: a real failure keeps cp's diagnostic. Why not `cp -n`/`--update=none`: they are GNU-only, and their exit status changed across coreutils releases.

Then run `node --test scripts/tests/subagent-mirror.test.mjs`: bash rows A to D pass.
implementationPlan.note: Changed only the control-checkout pre-flight mirror: capture failed cp diagnostics, count destination-exists failures as kept, otherwise print the diagnostic and exit 1. Preserved successful mirror counting, anchors/banner and task-worktree mirror. Fresh node --test scripts/tests/subagent-mirror.test.mjs exited 0: bash A-D pass (including all 60 real concurrent seat runs with byte equality), 6 PowerShell rows skipped under WSL as planned.

implementationPlan.description:
FIX the scripts/moe-agent.ps1 twin — epic parity rail, DoD 2. Edit the block under the same first comment (~line 949, before '# Normalize Command + CommandArgs').

Why: Copy-Item -Force overwrites rather than O_EXCL-creating, but an overlapping overwrite can still throw: a Windows CopyFile sharing violation, or .NET's exclusive file lock under pwsh on Unix. The script-wide $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop' then ends the seat.

Replace
            Copy-Item -Path $src -Destination $dest -Force
            $mirrored++
with
            try {
                Copy-Item -LiteralPath $src -Destination $dest -Force
            } catch {
                if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $dest)) { throw }
                $skipped++
                return
            }
            $mirrored++
Add an ASCII comment naming moe-agent.sh as the twin and stating the rule: a failed copy whose destination now exists lost to another seat; any other failure rethrows, so error handling for a real failure is unchanged. `return` inside the ForEach-Object block moves to the next file.

Use -LiteralPath only on the lines this step writes. task-3ad573a7 converts the block's other -Path sites; leave them to it. Keep the UTF-8 BOM (parity-check fails without it), LF endings, the first comment line, the banner and the end anchor.

Then run the Windows-node command from step 1: rows A, B and D pass on PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.
implementationPlan.note: Added the approved try/catch in the pre-flight mirror only: Copy-Item -LiteralPath failures count as kept only when Test-Path -LiteralPath sees the destination, otherwise rethrow. Fresh Windows-node suite exited 0: all 10 tests pass, no skips (Git Bash A-D, PowerShell 5.1 A/B/D, PowerShell 7 A/B/D). This proves the ForEach-Object return continues to the second file with mirrored=1/kept=1. PS1 BOM and LF endings retained; other -Path sites and prepare_worktree_launch untouched.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Seats that start in one project at the same moment all get through the pre-flight subagent mirror (.moe/agents/*.md -> <project>/.claude/agents/). In moe-agent.sh, a cp that fails while its destination exists afterwards lost GNU cp's O_EXCL create to another seat writing the same source bytes, and counts as kept. In moe-agent.ps1, a Copy-Item failure under the same condition (for example a sharing violation) counts as kept too. A copy failure that leaves no destination still stops the pre-flight as before: sh prints cp's own message and exits 1, and ps1 rethrows the same terminating error.
acceptanceCriteria: Row C of scripts/tests/subagent-mirror.test.mjs: 30 rounds of two concurrent real-cp mirrors into one fresh project; all 60 seat runs exit 0 and print the banner, and the bytes equal the sources. Before the fix it fails with 'File exists' (DoD 1).

Row A on every engine: a destination another seat created between the existence check and the copy yields 'Subagents: mirrored 1, kept 1 existing (.moe/agents/ -> .claude/agents/)' and exit 0 (DoD 2).
Row B on every engine: a copy failure that leaves no destination exits non-zero before the sentinel.
invariants: A failed copy counts as kept only when its destination exists after the failure.
The control-checkout mirror never overwrites an existing destination; user customizations win.
The banner text and the parity-check vocabulary are unchanged; moe-agent.ps1 keeps its UTF-8 BOM and LF endings.
prepare_worktree_launch's per-task W mirror is unchanged.
compatibility: A genuine mirror failure still ends the pre-flight with exit 1 (sh) or the same terminating error (ps1). No new codes or chat lines.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) A postflight.sh arm running two full wrappers through a PATH cp shim: rejected. The full harness takes ~20 min on WSL (mem:gotcha-qa-full-postflight-sh-runtime-and-summary-cap), and no PATH shim reaches a PowerShell cmdlet, so the ps1 twin would stay untested. Neither harness fixture even has .moe/agents, so no existing test runs this block. (2) Refactoring both blocks into functions for testability: unnecessary. seat-registration.test.mjs already slices top-level pre-flight segments by anchor text and runs them on bash, PS 5.1 and pwsh 7; this plan reuses that pattern. (3) The description's `cp … 2>/dev/null || [ -e "$dest" ] || <fail>`: adopted in spirit, with stderr captured so a real failure keeps cp's own diagnostic. (4) cp -n / --update=none: rejected; they are GNU-only and their exit status changed across coreutils releases. (5) A flock or mkdir lock around the mirror: rejected; stock macOS has no flock, and stale-lock handling is more code than the bug. (6) Leaving ps1 unchanged (mem:gotcha-wrapper-concurrent-seat-start-agents-mirror calls it unaffected): rejected. It has no EEXIST, but an overlapping Copy-Item -Force can still throw (a Windows CopyFile sharing violation, or .NET's exclusive lock on Unix), and EAP 'Stop' ends the seat. Seven lines give it the same 'destination exists => kept' rule, for the epic's parity rail and DoD 2.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- The sh block runs in EVERY seat's pre-flight against the control checkout's .claude/agents, before the loop and its claim, so it still races after the worktree flip. Its first comment line is unique in both wrappers, and no other test slice covers it: the seat-registration slices start at sh 2192 and ps1 1509.
- Architect measurement (WSL ext4, coreutils 9.4, two lockstep bash processes, six ~4 KB files): the unfixed loop lost 100 of 300 rounds, failing with exactly `cp: cannot create regular file … File exists`. The fixed loop had 0 failures in 600 seat runs, with bytes intact. GNU cp often OVERWRITES instead, because its own stat already saw the peer's file. So exact mirrored/kept counts can only be asserted under the injected race (row A); row C asserts exit codes, banner, sentinel and bytes.
- Windows has node.exe at /mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe, Git Bash at C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe and a Store pwsh.exe, so one Windows-node run from WSL covers Git Bash, PS 5.1 and pwsh 7. The task worktree under /mnt/d is reachable from Windows via wslpath -w.
- daemon-json-cap.test.mjs's CI-guard test requires that CI step's if: line to be exactly `if: runner.os != 'macOS'`; appending a file to the step's run line is safe.
planningNotes.risks:
- pwsh on Linux runs in CI only (WSL has no pwsh). The ps1 block joins '.claude\agents' with a backslash, which pwsh normalizes only through the provider. So the test's Copy-Item override and its checks use cmdlets (the module-qualified Microsoft.PowerShell.Management\Copy-Item, Test-Path -LiteralPath), never [IO.File], on wrapper-built paths.
- PS 5.1 reads a BOM-less temp .ps1 as ANSI, and the ps1 slice holds a non-ASCII arrow. Write temp ps1 files with a ﻿ BOM, as seat-registration does.
- task-3ad573a7 (WORKING, a ps1 -LiteralPath sweep) edits the same ps1 block. In worktree mode the later landing rebases; a hunk conflict parks on a rescue ref and is re-applied on the new tip, never auto-resolved. Using -LiteralPath on the lines this task writes keeps the overlap small.
- About 25 open rows edit moe-agent.sh/ps1 elsewhere (WT-1x, CQ-M07*, bug rows); this hunk is small and local.
- Row C is real concurrency. Bound every spin and wait, and kill only recorded PIDs (project rail).
- Keep the start anchor and both end anchors byte-identical; the test asserts each slice contains its copy call.

completionSummary: Fixed concurrent pre-flight subagent mirroring in Bash and PowerShell: copy failures count as kept only if the destination now exists; no-destination failures retain diagnostics and stop startup. Added real-block regression tests and CI wiring. RED reproduced Bash/Git Bash A+C and PS 5.1/7 A failures; GREEN final verification: WSL 4 pass/6 expected skips, Windows 10 pass/no skips, parity PASS. Both Bash engines verified 60 concurrent seats with intact bytes. Three scratch-only mutations failed their intended rows (A/C race, Bash B failure guard, both PS B failure guards). Worktree quality gate parity+lint passed; CI guard checks 2/2 and diff checks passed. Adversarial review complete; PS1 BOM/LF, existing customization skips, task-worktree mirror and WT-19b fixture preserved. Only four approved paths changed; handoff and gotcha recorded in Serena.
